speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an infant with recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing; can you describe exactly when these breathing difficulties occur, such as during feeding, crying, or specific positions?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia with possible co-existing Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD).

The symptoms of stridor and wheezing worsening with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with post-feed vomiting, are highly characteristic of this diagnosis. I will proceed to request an upper GI study to evaluate for reflux complications. REQUEST TEST: Upper GI_Series; REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Flexion_Stridor_Capture.
